name: Cardio Diagnostics Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Cardio Diagnostics Holdings is a Chicago-based micro-cap that develops AI-driven epigenetic and genetic blood tests for cardiovascular disease, led by its flagship Epi+Gen CHD test, which estimates a patient's three-year risk of a coronary heart disease event, and its PrecisionCHD test. The company was founded in 2017 on technology co-invented at the University of Iowa by CEO Meesha Dogan. Commercial traction is still minimal: trailing-twelve-month revenue through June 2026 was about $14,450 against a net loss of about $6.5M. The stock trades near $1.75 with a market cap of about $5.2M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The company has brought Epi+Gen CHD and PrecisionCHD to market, but revenue has not followed: FY2025 revenue was $14,825, down from $34,890 in FY2024 [2]. AI Deployment (2/2): Its AI-driven epigenetic risk tests are commercially available to clinicians, and the company has repositioned itself under the CDIO.AI brand as an 'AI-first' precision cardiovascular medicine company [4]. Market Share (0/2): Its share is negligible. Quarterly test revenue ranges from $2,680 to $7,475, and Q2 2026 revenue fell 28% YoY after the Family Medicine Specialists testing initiative ended [1]. Pipeline (0/2): Beyond onboarding new providers and an India partnership, no next-generation product with a specific launch date and revenue visibility was found [6]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $641K equals about 43 times revenue, far above the diagnostics-sector norm as a share of revenue, though small in absolute dollars [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): The stated aim of AI-powered precision medicine for preventing, detecting and managing cardiovascular disease is clear and founder-driven. CEO Meesha Dogan co-invented the core technology during her graduate studies [5]. The mission has not yet been validated by commercial execution. Community Impact (0/2): Apart from the India partnership, which the CEO framed as advancing 'equitable access' to cardiovascular care, no foundation, charitable program or quantified community investment was found [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found for the roughly 15-person workforce [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was found. Weighted shares outstanding moved from 26.9M in FY2024 to 1.75M in FY2025 and then to 2.96M in Q2 2026, which points to a reverse split followed by continued dilutive issuance rather than insider accumulation [1][2].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: average daily volume of 36,263 shares at $1.75 gives about $63K of daily dollar volume, far below the $1,000,000 minimum, so Infrastructure is 0 regardless of the other metrics [3]. The underlying metrics would also have scored poorly. TTM revenue of about $14,450 against a TTM net loss of about $6.47M gives a profit margin near -44,800%. ROE is about -87% on $7.43M of equity, and revenue fell 28.3% YoY in Q2 2026 ($5,360 vs $7,475) after a 57.5% decline in FY2025 [1][2]. The only positive is a clean balance sheet: $5.59M of cash against $370K of total debt, for D/E of about 5%. At a burn rate of roughly $1.5M to $1.8M per quarter, that cash covers only about 3 to 4 quarters before more financing is needed [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): The product is a CLIA-lab blood assay that reads DNA methylation and genotype data, a physical and regulated process that a software model cannot perform on its own [4]. The bigger threat is substitution. Cardiovascular risk scoring is a crowded field for AI, including AI-ECG and AI-CT plaque analytics from larger, better-funded players, and those tools could make a stand-alone epigenetic blood test unnecessary. With almost no revenue base, Cardio Diagnostics has little protection if clinicians adopt them. No analyst coverage was found that addresses this risk directly, which is itself a negative for a $5M company. AI Opportunity (1/1): All of the company's revenue, though trivial at about $14K TTM, comes from tests it markets as AI-driven [1][4].

infinite_game.summary: Cardio Diagnostics has a sincere, founder-led purpose: making heart-attack risk visible early enough to prevent it. In Sinek's terms, though, it is in survival mode. The cause has not survived a real test, the company has not had to pivot strategically, and repeated dilutive financing to cover a roughly $6.5M annual burn leaves little room for long-horizon decisions. The cause is real but too young and fragile to be called infinite.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The aim of preventing coronary heart disease through earlier, more precise risk detection is idealistic and service-oriented. It grew out of founder Meesha Dogan's University of Iowa research, which gives it some authenticity [5]. It has not yet shaped a durable organization or survived a leadership transition, and it currently reads more as a product description than a cause people sacrifice for.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The co-founder CEO has led the company continuously since 2017 and remains its technical inventor, which provides leadership continuity for a roughly 15-person team [3][5]. No turnover, engagement or culture data was found, so this scores as adequate rather than high-trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Company communications focus on promoting its own AI-first positioning [4]. No management commentary acknowledging competitors' strengths or describing learning from rivals in cardiovascular risk testing was found.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The company is too young and small to have faced a real existential pivot. Its main strategic moves so far are a rebrand to CDIO.AI and geographic expansion through an India partnership, which are incremental changes rather than reinvention [4][6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Management decisions are driven by survival. Opex was cut from $8.4M in FY2024 to $6.5M in FY2025, and R&D spending remains small in absolute terms [2]. The share count trajectory points to repeated dilutive capital raises [1][2]. No costly, principled long-term bet beyond keeping the company funded is evident.

investment_thesis: The bull case rests on a credible scientific idea: an AI-interpreted epigenetic blood test, Epi+Gen CHD, that estimates three-year heart-attack risk and could fit into preventive cardiology and employer wellness programs [4]. The balance sheet is debt-light, with $5.59M of cash against $370K of total debt and $7.43M of equity at Q2 2026 [1]. The company is still onboarding new providers after the Family Medicine Specialists initiative ended and is pursuing an India partnership to scale access [1][6]. At a $5.2M market cap, any meaningful reimbursement win or channel partnership would be large relative to the company's size [3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is overwhelming. TTM revenue is about $14,450 against a net loss of about $6.47M, and FY2025 revenue fell 57.5% to $14,825 [1][2]. Five years after its 2022 Nasdaq listing, the product shows no commercial traction. Quarterly cash burn of $1.5M to $1.8M against $5.59M of cash leaves roughly 3 to 4 quarters of runway. The share count path (26.9M weighted shares in FY2024, about 1.75M after an apparent reverse split, then 2.96M by Q2 2026) points to ongoing dilution [1][2]. Average daily volume of about 36,000 shares, roughly $63K a day, puts the stock far below IOWN's $1M liquidity floor, so it cannot be traded responsibly at portfolio scale [3].
key_catalysts: Onboarding of new provider channels to replace the expired Family Medicine Specialists heart-attack-prevention program, the main driver of the 28% YoY Q2 2026 revenue decline [1]
Expansion in India through a partnership that management says will broaden access to its AI-driven cardiovascular tests [6]
Q3 2026 results, expected around November 6, 2026, which will show whether quarterly revenue can stay above the Q2 level of $5,360 [1]
key_risks: Going-concern and dilution risk: about $1.5M to $1.8M of quarterly net losses against $5.59M of cash implies more equity raises within about a year, after an apparent reverse split already shrank the share count from 26.9M to about 1.75M [1][2]
Commercial failure risk: FY2025 revenue of $14,825 was down 57.5% YoY, showing the tests have not achieved reimbursement-driven adoption [2]
Liquidity risk: about $63K of daily dollar volume, far below IOWN's $1M floor, makes position entry and exit impractical [3]
